newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia 1997 coffee output said down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia 1997 coffee output said down sharply.

text.p: Indonesia's coffee production is expected to plunge by 160,000 tonnes to 290,000 tonnes in 1997, Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters told Reuters on Wednesday.
He said the exportable amount in 1997 was expected to fall to 180,000 tonnes from 330,000 tonnes in 1996.
"The forecast is based on information I obtained during a meeting with exporters from key production centres today in Jakarta, where they were attending a coffee seminar," he said.

"The situation in Indonesia is critical. It is very difficult to buy in the (coffee growing) districts...there are not enough beans," Soedargo said, adding that production in 1996 was around 450,000 tonnes.
He said stock levels were low because exporters had shipped their beans when prices in international markets were booming.
Soedargo said the production shortfall was due to incessant rains and strong winds that affected flowering and fruiting.
He said some exporters informed him that they felt 1997 production could fall as much as 50 percent from last year.
